decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Mr.Martin' in turn 1, establishing B's name. This is a straightforward explicit fact.
The word 'again' in 'We hope you'll visit Beijing again' (turn 5) is a clear presupposition that B has visited Beijing before. This is an E1 presupposition from the utterance itself.

Turn 5 alone ('visit Beijing again') presupposes B has been to Beijing before, but does not directly establish B is currently there. The 'currently in Beijing' conclusion requires cross-turn inference from turns 7 and 9, which is better captured by c8. As a standalone claim from the cited evidence, it overreaches.
decisions.counterexample: B could be in a different city, and A is referencing a past visit while B is about to travel elsewhere.

decisions.claim: B is about to board a vehicle (plane/train/ship)
decisions.reason: Turn 7 'It's almost time to get aboard' directly states B is about to board a vehicle. This is explicit and unambiguous.

decisions.claim: B is going on a journey
decisions.reason: Turn 9 'Have a pleasant journey' directly establishes B is going on a journey. This is an explicit fact about B.

decisions.claim: B is addressed as Mr. Martin
decisions.reason: c6 ('B is addressed as Mr. Martin') and c1 ('B's name is Mr. Martin') refer to the same fact from the same evidence. Being addressed as Mr. Martin establishes B's name. c1 is the more canonical statement.

decisions.claim: B has been in Beijing (is currently visiting or has visited)
decisions.reason: c7 ('B has been in Beijing') is essentially equivalent to c2 ('B has visited Beijing before'). Both derive from the same presupposition in turn 5. c2 is more precise.

Combining turn 5 ('visit Beijing again') with turn 7 ('time to get aboard') and the overall departure context (turns 1, 9) yields a well-grounded inference that B is departing from Beijing. This is a necessary cross-turn inference.
c9 ('B is on a journey/trip') and c5 ('B is going on a journey') are bidirectionally equivalent, both derived from turn 9's 'Have a pleasant journey.' c5 is the canonical choice.

decisions.claim: B has relationships with people in Beijing who will miss B's departure
decisions.reason: Turn 3 'We'll miss you. I hope we'll keep in touch' presupposes that A (and possibly others in Beijing) have a relationship with B and will miss B's departure. The 'we' and 'keep in touch' imply existing relationships. This is a well-grounded inference.
